title: [CQ-M07j1] Seat job forward over the daemon's /mcp
description:
SPIDR split out of CQ-M07j (task-1dc49ae27e22494a95e15ada3e9c1fe9) by architect-b520bc90 on 2026-11-01, as that row anticipated: "Expect a SPIDR split at planning if the forward transport needs its own slice". CQ-M07j's runSeatJob passes this forward to runAgentJob. Depends on CQ-M07i (task-18809c69), which creates the two files this edits.

**Decision: forward over the daemon's /mcp (the moe-proxy path), never /runner.**
- The /runner channel (runner-client.mjs) gives every call the authenticated runner identity (McpAdapter options.runner). record_check_dispatch trusts that identity as runner-attested evidence. A guest agent's calls must never carry runner trust: if the bridge allowlist ever grew, that would be a confused deputy.
- The bridge already scopes every guest request before forward sees it:
  - guest-bridge.mjs TOOLS gives an exact per-role allowlist and stamps the binding's taskId/workerId;
  - guest-session.mjs STAMPED adds sessionId/attemptId/generation.
  That mirrors what moe-proxy does on /mcp.
- runAgentJob's own moe.acquire_resource/release_resource go through the same forward under the binding's taskId, so the job lease stays task-keyed.

Objective: export `seatForward(projectPath, { WebSocketImpl = globalThis.WebSocket, timeoutMs = 30_000 } = {})` from scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs. It returns `forward(tool, args, { signal })`.
- Each call opens ONE socket to ws://<loopback host>:<port>/mcp of this project's daemon. readDaemonInfo (vm-control.mjs) supplies the port and host: it is bounded, refuses on a project mismatch, and admits only a loopback bind proven by /health.
- It sends one JSON-RPC tools/call { name: tool, arguments: args } and resolves the daemon's RAW `result` object unchanged ({ content: [...] }). guest-mcp-shim.py relays frame.result verbatim as the agent's MCP tools/call result, so it must never be the parsed inner text, which is what vm-control's mcpCaller and runner-client's call return.
- An error reply, a close or error event, the timeout or an aborted signal (already aborted, or aborting mid-call) rejects with one fixed code. runGuestSession maps any rejection to BRIDGE_UPSTREAM_FAILED and never echoes it. The socket closes in finally on every path.
- It sends no headers and never reads the runner key file.

NOT in scope: runSeatJob and the seat-job CLI (CQ-M07j), and the wrappers (CQ-M07m/n).

Verification: in a git-archive snapshot (mem:gotcha-local-runner-tests recipe) with this task's files overlaid: env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-seat.test.mjs
definitionOfDone: forward sends exactly one tools/call {name, arguments} per call over ws://127.0.0.1 (or [::1]):<daemon.json port>/mcp of this project and resolves the daemon's raw result object unchanged (rows with a fake WebSocket, VC-M1 style).
An error reply, a close, an error event, the timeout, and a signal aborted before or during the call each reject with a fixed code, and the socket is closed on every path (rows).
No runner key is read or sent: the fake WebSocket sees no headers argument, and a runner key dir pointed at a missing path changes nothing (row).
A daemon.json for another project or a non-loopback /health bind refuses before any socket opens (row, reusing readDaemonInfo).
The named test passes in a git-archive snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:
seatForward in scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs.
FILE NOTE: agent-seat.mjs and scripts/tests/local-runner-seat.test.mjs are CREATED BY CQ-M07i (task-18809c69, this row's dependsOn). They are listed as newFiles only because they did not exist when this plan was written; by the time this row is claimable they exist. EDIT them with the Edit/Write tools, never recreate or overwrite M07i's startSeat/stopSeat/runAgentSeat bytes. CQ-M07j also declares both paths, so a shell write would leave them HELD at landing. Read mem:gotcha-local-runner-tests first (forbidden-pattern literals, numstat counting).

export function seatForward(projectPath, { WebSocketImpl = globalThis.WebSocket, timeoutMs = 30_000 } = {}) returns forward(tool, args, { signal }). Reuse readDaemonInfo from ./vm-control.mjs (add it to M07i's existing vm-control import). It is the bounded, no-follow daemon.json read that refuses another project and admits only a /health-proven loopback bind. Per call, in this order:
(1) const id = ++lastId (one counter per forward, captured locally: concurrent calls must each match their own id). Refuse before any read, inside the same try that maps every failure to the fixed code: a third argument whose signal is neither undefined nor an AbortSignal; an already-aborted signal; a WebSocketImpl that is not a function. Serialize the frame { jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method: 'tools/call', params: { name: tool, arguments: args } } now, so a non-serializable args refuses before any read or socket.
(2) await readDaemonInfo(projectPath), fresh on every call because the daemon may restart on a new port. Any throw refuses.
(3) Re-check signal.aborted after that await: an abort that landed during the /health probe refuses with no socket. From here to the abort-listener registration everything is synchronous, so no abort can slip in between.
(4) Inside one Promise:
  - Start the timeoutMs timer (a backstop for a caller without a signal; an invalid delay becomes 1 ms in Node, so it fails closed).
  - Add the abort listener with { once: true }.
  - Construct exactly new WebSocketImpl(url) with ONE argument. url is ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp, or ws://[::1]:<port>/mcp when host is '::1' (mcpCaller's spelling). No protocols, no options, no headers. This module never imports runner-client.mjs and never reads a runner key. A constructor throw refuses.
  - 'open' sends the frame once.
  - 'message': non-JSON data refuses. A reply whose id is not this call's is ignored. A reply with an own `error` member, or whose `result` is not a plain object, refuses. Otherwise resolve reply.result itself: the RAW { content: [...] } object, never content[0].text parsed. guest-mcp-shim.py relays frame.result verbatim, agent-lifecycle leaseCall parses content itself, and runGuestSession checks isError itself.
  - 'close' and 'error' refuse; so do the timer and the abort listener.
(5) .finally: clearTimeout; signal?.removeEventListener('abort', ...), because runGuestSession passes ONE long-lived session signal to every forward and a leaked listener per call accumulates; socket?.close() inside try/catch.
error handling: every refusal is ONE fixed code, SEAT_FORWARD_FAILED, with a fixed message ('Seat forward failed.'). It never carries the daemon's message or codeName, a path, a key or the args. Every listener body is total: Node reports a throwing EventTarget listener as an uncaughtException (verified on Node 24). runGuestSession maps any rejection to BRIDGE_UPSTREAM_FAILED and never echoes it.
Header: add 3-5 lines on seatForward.
- It goes over /mcp (the moe-proxy path), never /runner. A /runner call carries the authenticated runner identity (McpAdapter options.runner), which record_check_dispatch trusts as runner-attested evidence, and a guest's calls must never carry it.
- The bridge's TOOLS allowlist and STAMPED identity already scope every guest request, as moe-proxy does.
- runAgentJob's acquire/release_resource go through the same forward under the binding's taskId, so the job lease stays task-keyed.
- It needs Node 22+'s global WebSocket; without one, every call refuses.
NOT here: runSeatJob and the seat-job CLI (CQ-M07j), the wrappers (CQ-M07m/n), any vm-control.mjs change.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this diff, as the final step (load adversarial-self-review). Check:
1. Can any path open a socket before readDaemonInfo has proven this project's loopback daemon in the same call, or after the signal aborted?
2. Does any call open more than one socket or send more than one frame? Does any path leave a socket open, a timer pending or an abort listener attached?
3. Can any rejection carry the daemon's message, a codeName, a path, the args or a key? Is the code always SEAT_FORWARD_FAILED?
4. Does anything pass a second argument to the WebSocket constructor, import runner-client.mjs or read MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR?
5. Is the resolved value the daemon's raw result object, never the parsed inner text?
6. Can any listener throw? Node's EventTarget turns that into an uncaughtException.
7. With two concurrent calls on one forward, does each match only its own id?
8. Did M07i's startSeat/stopSeat/runAgentSeat bytes and its AS rows stay untouched?
If any byte changes, re-run step 3's exact command and submit that fresh output.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of the two-file diff, all 8 checks.
1. No socket opens before readDaemonInfo proves the loopback daemon in the same call, and none opens after an abort (pre-check, then re-check after the await).
2. One socket and one frame per call. The finally clears the timer, removes the abort listener and closes the socket on every path.
3. Every rejection is the fixed SEAT_FORWARD_FAILED with the fixed message, including a throwing options.signal getter.
4. The constructor gets the URL alone. runner-client.mjs is not imported and MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR is not read.
5. The resolved value is reply.result itself, never the parsed text.
6. Every listener body is total.
7. Ids are a local taken before any await, so concurrent calls match only their own reply (SF1).
8. M07i's startSeat, stopSeat and runAgentSeat bytes and its AS0-AS6 rows are untouched. The only M07i lines changed are the header comment and the vm-control import.

One real finding, fixed: options?.signal was read before the try, so a throwing getter would have rejected with a raw error. It now sits inside the try, with a new SF2 row. A scratch mutant that moves it back fails SF2.

Theoretical, documented and not fixed:
- An abort or timeout closes the socket, but a tools/call the daemon already dispatched keeps running, as with moe-proxy.
- An abort during the /health probe settles only after that probe, at most 5 s.

Step 3's exact command was re-run after the fix: 11 tests, 11 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. Numstat: +48/-1 and +128/-2 = 179 of 400.

From CQ-V12's whole-epic review (task-b621ddc9, worker-0e1ab990, 2026-11-01): this row's design note says guest-session.mjs STAMPED "adds sessionId/attemptId/generation. That mirrors what moe-proxy does on /mcp". That holds only for get_context/start_step/complete_step/complete_task.

- Since CQ-V06a, moe-proxy also stamps qa_approve and qa_reject (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:337).
- guest-session.mjs:32 does not, and guest-bridge forbids a guest to send the keys.
- So through this forward, a VM QA seat's qa_approve/qa_reject on a verified-local task is always refused (STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED).

Filed as task-5464e725 (bug, MEDIUM, CQ-V epic). The worker side of this forward is unaffected.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs exports seatForward(projectPath, { WebSocketImpl = globalThis.WebSocket, timeoutMs = 30_000 } = {}), which returns forward(tool, args, { signal }).

Each call proves this project's loopback daemon through vm-control readDaemonInfo. It then opens ONE socket, with no headers, to ws://127.0.0.1 (or [::1]):<port>/mcp, sends one tools/call { name, arguments } and resolves the daemon's raw result object unchanged.

These all reject with the one fixed code SEAT_FORWARD_FAILED: an error reply, a non-object result, unparsable data, a close or error event, the timeout, a refused daemon.json or /health, and an abort before or during the call. On every path the socket, the timer and the abort listener are released.

It never uses /runner and never reads a runner key.
invariants: A guest call never reaches /runner and never carries a runner key or any header: the WebSocket constructor gets exactly one argument, the URL.
No socket opens unless the signal is live and readDaemonInfo proved this project's loopback daemon in the same call.
One socket and one tools/call frame per call. On every path the socket is closed, the timer cleared and the abort listener removed.
Every rejection is SEAT_FORWARD_FAILED with a fixed message: no upstream text, path, args or key.
The resolved value is the daemon's raw result, never the parsed text.
compatibility: CQ-M07i's startSeat, stopSeat and runAgentSeat, and its AS rows, are unchanged.
vm-control.mjs (readDaemonInfo, mcpCaller) is used unchanged. seatForward(project) is the shape CQ-M07j's runSeatJob passes to runAgentJob.
runGuestSession (BRIDGE_UPSTREAM_FAILED on any rejection, its own isError check) and agent-lifecycle leaseCall (parses content itself) consume the raw result as is.
approvedScope: agent-seat.mjs: export seatForward(projectPath, { WebSocketImpl, timeoutMs }) returning forward(tool, args, { signal }); the readDaemonInfo import; 3-5 header lines.
local-runner-seat.test.mjs: rows SF1-SF4 and their sf* helpers.
reuse: readDaemonInfo (vm-control.mjs) supplies the daemon.json bounds, the project match and the /health loopback proof.

The socket pattern follows vm-control mcpCaller. A new function is still needed: mcpCaller parses content[0].text, maps the daemon's codeName and takes no signal, and vm-control.mjs stays outside this slice.
sourceAssumptions: vm-control.mjs readDaemonInfo(projectPath) resolves {port, host: '127.0.0.1'|'::1'} only after three checks: a bounded no-follow regular daemon.json, a canonicalProjectPath match, and a loopbackDaemonHost /health proof. Any refusal throws DAEMON_UNREACHABLE.
McpAdapter.handleSingle answers tools/call without an initialize, with { jsonrpc, id, result: { content: [{ type: 'text', text }] } } or { jsonrpc, id, error: { code, message, data } }.
WebSocketServer.isAllowedUpgradeOrigin admits an absent Origin. Node 24's global WebSocket sends no Origin header (probed 2026-11-01), and vm-control mcpCaller already dials /mcp the same way.
WebSocketServer.cleanupMcpWorkers on a /mcp close only cancels waiters registered on that socket. moe-proxy also opens one connection per call.

guest-session.mjs reply() calls forward(scoped.tool, args, { signal: session.controller.signal }) under bounded(). It maps any rejection, and clean.isError, to BRIDGE_UPSTREAM_FAILED. guest-mcp-shim.py relays frame['result'] verbatim.
agent-lifecycle.mjs leaseCall destructures { isError, content } from forward's result and parses content[0].text itself.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Forward over /runner via runner-client.mjs: rejected. Its socket carries the authenticated runner identity, which record_check_dispatch trusts as runner-attested evidence. A guest's calls must never carry it, or a widened bridge allowlist becomes a confused deputy.
2. Reusing vm-control mcpCaller: rejected. It parses content[0].text, which breaks guest-mcp-shim.py's verbatim relay and leaseCall. It maps the daemon's codeName and takes no signal. Changing it would edit vm-control.mjs, outside this slice.
3. A tool allowlist inside forward: rejected. /mcp carries no authority beyond any loopback client's. The bridge's TOOLS/STAMPED already scope guest requests, and runAgentJob's lease calls are fixed.
4. One persistent socket: rejected. Per-call sockets match moe-proxy, survive a daemon restart on a new port, and make close-on-every-path trivial.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The daemon /mcp needs no initialize. Success is result.content[0].text; failure is a JSON-RPC error.
- Node 24's global WebSocket sends no Origin header, which the daemon would refuse.
- runGuestSession already probes /health before each forward (daemonRefusal). seatForward probes again because leaseCall has no probe of its own; the double probe is intentional.
- Node turns a throwing EventTarget listener into an uncaughtException.
- getEventListeners(signal, 'abort') can observe listener cleanup.
planningNotes.risks:
- Listener leak: runGuestSession reuses ONE session signal for every forward, so a missing removeEventListener accumulates and warns.
- Id capture: the id must be a local taken before the await, or concurrent calls cross-match.
- An abort during the /health probe settles only after the probe (at most 5 s, loopbackDaemonHost's default). The post-await check covers it with no socket.
- Mutation resistance: event rows need a large timeoutMs plus a test timeout, or the timer masks a dropped listener.
- Size: about 45 runtime plus 160 test lines, so the 400-line cap is not at risk.
